bundle.text:
# Installable overlay / custom-base patch for `@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers`.
# This monorepo's official `dsh-base` does not mount the row; prefer:
#   dsh plugin --profile web add @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers
# Some fork product bases already insert `id: superpowers` — do not stack a
# second install on those bases (disable the base row first, or omit this patch).
- insert:
    - id: superpowers
      name: '@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers'

readme.text:
---
description: "obra/superpowers skills provider plus a system-prompt bootstrap for DeepSeek Harness."
kind: "package-bundle"
---
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Bring the obra/superpowers workflow kernel and its fused extensions into a DeepSeek Harness profile as one skill catalog plus a standing skill-first bootstrap. Use it when product sessions should move from intent through plan, test, debug, review, and verification in a repeatable order. It is opt-in and ships no harness peers.

- [Summary](#summary)
- [Model Experience](#model-experience)
- [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work)
- [Dev Note](#dev-note)

Installable DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle that brings [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) into product sessions: a **35-skill** catalog split into core, advanced, product, and authoring bundles, adapted to dsh tooling, plus a SessionStart-equivalent bootstrap. The default profile loads the 19-skill core bundle (`diagnosing-superpowers` stays out until a deep dsh port).

Publish name: `@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers` (version tracks the harness family, currently `0.1.0-rc.41`). Source of record for this fork package: [github.com/oThTJx/dsh-superpowers](https://github.com/oThTJx/dsh-superpowers). This package is opt-in and is not part of the official main `dsh-base` composition.

| Superpowers behavior | dsh realization |
|---|---|
| Skills library under `skills/*/SKILL.md` | `ctx.skills` provider `superpowers` (packaged `skills/` directory, dsh-adapted) |
| SessionStart hook injecting `using-superpowers` | `system-prompt/assemble` section `skill:superpowers` with the same `<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>` framing (every non-subagent request); `using-superpowers` is user-only in the skill catalog |
| Platform `references/*-tools.md` | bundled `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md` appended inside that section |
| Subagent skip (`SUBAGENT-STOP`) | no full `using-superpowers` bootstrap when `session.header.origin === 'subagent'`; injects a short `skill:superpowers-worker` preamble instead |
| Model loads other skills on demand | existing `dsh-tool-skill` catalog + `skill` tool |

The skill bodies ship as dsh-adapted prose under `skills/` (no vendored source, no git submodule). Foreign-harness tool names and platform references were rewritten for dsh, and the `superpowers:` skill-name prefix was removed. The published tarball includes `skills/`, `assets/NOTICE.md`, and the offline scorer `scripts/score-skill-first.mjs`. NOTICE records obra/superpowers (`2ce8aa15`, v7.0.1), mattpocock/skills (`5beb35b0`), addyosmani/agent-skills (`aeac41d4`), and bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD (`61e01f82`, with trademark notice) as review pins.

Capabilities that overlap are fused into **one** owning skill. When an upstream source has material that does not justify a second skill directory, it ships as a **reference pack** under the owner and is loaded only at the step that needs it. The catalog therefore stays at 35 skills while the fused behavior keeps growing.
The package ships four bundles. `core` is always loaded; the others are opt-in through the `bundles` config.

| Bundle | Default | Skills | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core` | yes | 19 | The day-to-day workflow: brainstorming, planning, execution, TDD, debugging, review, verification, finish, domain/design, security, sources, constraints |
| `advanced` | no | 6 | Subagent-driven execution and parallel dispatch, context engineering, prototype, wizard, grilling |
| `product` | no | 8 | Idea, PRFAQ, PRD, spec, UX, retrospective, course correction, and multi-role debate for multi-stakeholder product work |
| `authoring` | no | 2 | `writing-skills` and `dsh-harness-contributor` for skill and repository maintainers |

Core is always included, even when `bundles` names only an optional bundle. A bare install therefore sees 19 skills; a full install sees 35. The model-visible core catalog is 16 skills after `using-superpowers`, `handoff`, and `wait-what` stay user-only.

Superpowers remains the workflow kernel (`brainstorming` → `writing-plans` → TDD / debugging / review / verify). Selected [mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills), [addyosmani/agent-skills](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills), and [BMAD-METHOD](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD) practices ship as one fused catalog: every skill declares at most one `bundle` label, and that label is the only catalog metadata this provider publishes.

Session skills (`grilling`, `handoff`, `wait-what`) are absent from the model `<available_skills>` catalog and refused by the model `skill` tool. Users invoke them with a whitespace-bounded `/name` token in a user message (for example `/grilling`); `dsh-tool-skill` injects the skill body as instructions. `using-superpowers` is also `disable-model-invocation: true`, but its standing copy arrives through the system-prompt bootstrap rather than that gesture (users may still `/using-superpowers` to reload the body without the adapter).

Obra skills that absorbed merges (keep on obra sync): `brainstorming` (inline Architectural grilling; Not Doing; Always/Ask/Never; reject aim-past-100), `using-superpowers` (≤5-line intent fork; anti-stack; tiny-edit; implementation priority; contextual gates), `test-driven-development`, `systematic-debugging`, `requesting-code-review` (Standards ∥ Spec + checklists + review lenses + doubt pass), `executing-plans` (slice discipline + impact map), `refactoring` (clarity + structural modes), `source-driven-development` (research mode), `codebase-design`, `writing-plans`, `handoff`, `verification-before-completion`.

Implementation and quality extensions: `executing-plans` owns the task loop, slice discipline, and impact map; `refactoring` owns clarity and structural modes; `source-driven-development` owns API-grounded work and the research mode; `requesting-code-review` owns post-hoc review and the in-flight doubt pass; `subagent-driven-development` owns per-task dispatch and parallel-dispatch reference. `dsh-harness-contributor` and `explaining-changes` live in the authoring and advanced bundles and do not enter the default core catalog.
`bundle` is catalog metadata only — not a router. Invocation frontmatter is parsed privately by this provider (plugin-only; upstream harness packages unchanged).

Each skill owns one capability, and every selected source that covers that capability feeds its body. When two sources overlap, the package keeps **one** skill and merges both contributions — it never ships two peers for one job, and it does not drop a selected source's behaviour because another source moved first. Unselected capabilities are listed as out of scope in the debt table.

| Skill | Sources fused into it | It owns |
|---|---|---|
| `brainstorming` | obra spine · BMAD product scheme · agent-skills anti-patterns | intent → approved design, size-based gates |
| `writing-plans` | obra plan format · agent-skills task breakdown · Matt spec-to-tickets | approved spec → ordered plan |
| `test-driven-development` | obra Iron Law · agent-skills trigger breadth | RED-GREEN-REFACTOR loop |
| `subagent-driven-development` | obra controller · dsh settlement wait · parallel dispatch | per-task dispatch, review, and parallel investigation |
| `executing-plans` | obra inline execution · agent-skills slicing rules · dsh script wiring | inline plan execution, slice discipline, impact map |
| `systematic-debugging` | obra four phases · agent-skills error recovery · observability and performance | root cause before any fix |
| `refactoring` | agent-skills clarity body · dsh structural extension · agent-skills deprecation/migration | clarity and structural modes, retirement |
| `requesting-code-review` | obra Standards ∥ Spec · agent-skills quality body · BMAD review lenses · in-flight doubt pass | review request, lenses, and disposition |
| `verification-before-completio
The map is an inventory, not a lock: a skill may gain a source, but it never splits into one peer per source, and a merged section is never replaced by whichever upstream moved last.

The following capabilities ship behind their owner rather than as extra skill directories. The owner links the pack at the step that needs it, so the model pays for the material only when that branch is reached.

| Owner | Reference | Fuses |
|---|---|---|
| `systematic-debugging` | `references/observability-and-performance.md` | production observability · performance regression workflow |
| `refactoring` | `references/clarity.md` | behavior-preserving clarity pass |
| `refactoring` | `references/structural.md` | structural change after repeated fixes |
| `refactoring` | `references/deprecation-and-migration.md` | deprecation decision · strangler/adapter/flag · expand → contract |
| `executing-plans` | `references/slice-discipline.md` | slice loop · slicing strategies · scope discipline |
| `executing-plans` | `references/impact-analysis.md` | short impact map before a cross-boundary change |
| `ux-spec` | `references/frontend-engineering.md` | component and state ownership · design-system adherence · accessibility · responsive UI |
| `context-engineering` | `references/project-context.md` | `AGENTS.md` setup/adopt/refresh/audit · writing for agents |
| `codebase-design` | `references/architecture-spine.md` | architecture invariants · stable `AD` IDs · reviewer gate; plus TypeScript entry-point enforcement in the body |
| `writing-plans` | `references/spec-to-tickets.md` | spec-driven workf

Reference packs are part of the owner's contract: `tests/superpowers.spec.ts` checks that each fusion pack listed above ships with its defining pins, that every reference file is linked from its owner's prose, and that every relative Markdown link under `skills/` resolves. A pack is not a second router and does not appear in `<available_skills>`.

Requires DeepSeek Harness peers (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill` and related packages), typically from the official CLI/`dsh-base` stack. Source-workspace `workspace:*` peers mean the matching DSH release; packed manifests substitute that exact version. DSH checks those peer ranges at install and profile startup and refuses an incompatible pair without an exact version exemption — see [Version compatibility](#version-compatibility).

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers
```

From a harness source tree:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers
```

Then boot `dsh --profile web` (or `pnpm dsh web`). If this fork's `dsh-base` already mounts `id: superpowers`, do not add the same row again — disable the base row first, or use a profile that does not include it.

```sh
pnpm run build:lib:host
pnpm --filter @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers pack
pnpm dsh plugin --profile superpowers-demo add ./firefly0621-dsh-superpowers-0.1.0-rc.41.tgz
```

(`pnpm pack` writes the tarball to the repository root by default. There is no per-package `build` script; host lib build produces `lib/`.)

readme.text:
This package is opt-in in the harness source tree. Mount the shipped overlay patch (or `dsh plugin add`):

```sh
pnpm dsh web --patch packages/skill/superpowers/cordis.patch.yml
pnpm dsh --profile headless --patch packages/skill/superpowers/cordis.patch.yml "task"
```

Fork trees that already mount `id: superpowers` in their base need no extra step; set `disabled: true` on that row to omit it.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `skillsRoot` | packaged `skills/` directory | Absolute skills directory; a relative path fails at apply |
| `bootstrap` | `true` | Contribute parent `using-superpowers` (+ dsh adapter) as `skill:superpowers`, and the short worker preamble as `skill:superpowers-worker` on subagent-origin sessions |
| `bundles` | `['core']` | Bundles to expose: `core` is always included; add `advanced`, `product`, and/or `authoring` |

Example full install:

```yaml
- id: superpowers
  name: '@firefly0621/dsh-superpowers'
  config:
    bundles: [core, advanced, product, authoring]

There is no vendored submodule. To re-port newer upstream releases: for each source, diff **content baseline → target**, then walk every open row in **sync debt** below, then re-apply the dsh adaptation by hand. Do **not** use `assets/NOTICE.md` review pins as the sole diff baseline — those pins record last review, not “skills/ equals that tree”.

Adaptation rules: replace foreign-harness tool names and platform references, remove the `superpowers:` skill-name prefix, **keep the behavioral content verbatim** (dsh exceptions only in the table below), and distill Matt / agent-skills / BMAD ADDs (never dump BMAD `_bmad` runtime, memlog, HTML seals, or trademark personas).

Since the v7.0.1 sync, `subagent-driven-development` and `writing-skills` keep their long guidance in `references/` and read a file from disk at the step that needs it, so a compacted session can reload one section instead of losing the whole body. Keep that layout when re-porting: a rule that lives inline again defeats it. The same sync removed the `executing-plans` worked example for the same reason, and rebuilt `brainstorming` onto the v7.0.1 text (which already carries `961a26d`): first message → conversation → playback → size the work, a design doc at every size (a short one for a small change), and a gate that never skips without consent. The dsh decision-support format for architectural clarifying stays inline and states its one-question exception; the older three-path router and its separate gate tables are gone so one gate is stated once. Every packaged `SKILL.md` stays under upstream's 20,000-byte compaction cut, and the package suite enforces it.

**Fusion, not port.** Several upstreams feed one skill, and each keeps its own role: obra supplies the behavioral spine, agent-skills supplies ADDs and OPTIMIZE merges, Matt supplies named extensions, BMAD supplies product-discovery distillations. Never replace a merged section with one upstream's version because that upstream moved — re-apply the merge onto the new spine and keep every selected source's contribution (for example `brainstorming` keeps Not Doing / Always·Ask·Never through the v7 rebuild, and `test-driven-development` keeps the agent-skills trigger breadth inside obra's description). When the contribution is a distinct capability rather than a replacement section, add a reference pack under the owner; do not create a second skill directory for it. Capabilities outside the selected scope are named as out of scope in the debt table rather than silently counted as ported.

| Exception | Why |
|---|---|
| Strip `superpowers:` / foreign skill-name prefixes | Catalog names are bare in dsh |
| Rewrite foreign harness tools → dsh (`subagent` / `subagent_fork`, `todo_write`, `dsh-tools.md`) | Platform adapter |
| `writing-plans` handoff label `Native` → `Inline` | Avoid “native harness” ambiguity; still means same-session `executing-plans` |
| `sdd-workspace`: refuse marker-less existing dirs (no adopt) | Deliberate ownership tighten vs obra; documented in the script header |
| Invoke bundled scripts via `bash …` | Packaged extractors may strip Unix exec bits |
| Keep catalog `Do not use` negatives / description contracts | Fusion routing gates |

| Source | Content baseline (landed in `skills/`) | NOTICE review pin | Open sync debt |
|---|---|---|---|
| obra/superpowers | Spine through v7.0.1 at `2ce8aa15`, with `brainstorming` following the v7.0.1 text (which already carries `961a26d`): first message → conversation → playback → size the work, a design doc at every size, never skip without consent, one red-flag table, no three-path router; `subagent-driven-development` / `writing-skills` guidance split into `references/`, the `executing-plans` worked example removed for the compaction cut, inline task loop kept (`scripts/task-start` / `task-done`); review-lens and walkthrough distillations landed in existing owners; bundled scripts carry the post-baseline task-ID, unclosed-fence, Windows-path, and relative-`--project-dir` fixes | `2ce8aa15` (v7.0.1) plus the post-baseline fixes `f75c01f`, `750ba92`, `3735a50`, `bb3a5aa`, `fa50d83`, `8b0eefc`, with `369bd87` re-expressed; `961a26d`, `2b2ef34`, `c7730f7`, and `6ff820e` are already in `2ce8aa15`, and `699edc6` deletes a test harness absent from that tree | *(none)* for the selected obra spine; `diagnosing-superpowers` and cross-harness reference material stay in Known Limitati

1. Catalog length stays **35**; each skill carries at most one `bundle` label, the default core catalog is **19** skills, and no skill declares a removed `tier` label; no second meta-router; no `bmad-*` skill directory names.
2. Re-assert OPTIMIZE merges (brainstorming Scheme B / Not Doing / Always·Ask·Never; TDD; review Standards ∥ Spec; grilling user-only; executing slice/impact; refactoring clarity/structural pins) after any obra spine overwrite.
3. Same-name overlaps from agent-skills (`refactoring`, `test-driven-development`) OPTIMIZE in place — do not add peer directories; merged skills keep their capability as references under the owner.
4. Update `SEMANTIC_DESCRIPTION_GROUPS` / `NEGATIVE_BOUNDARY_BANNED` when obra changes skill routing semantics (for example `executing-plans` inline vs `subagent-driven-development`).
5. Bump NOTICE **review** pins when you re-read upstream; update the **content baseline / debt** table when landed content or debt changes; keep ADD `Do not use when…` and BMAD exit-state pins.
6. Run `pnpm exec vitest run packages/skill/superpowers/tests/superpowers.spec.ts`.
7. Confirm `executing-plans` ships `scripts/task-start` and `scripts/task-done` and t

**Preserve on obra sync:** Matt-added skill directories (`domain-modeling`, `codebase-design`, `prototype`, `wizard`, `grilling`, `handoff`, `wait-what` and companions); agent-skills / BMAD ADD directories (`constraint-driven-development`, `source-driven-development`, `context-engineering`, `security-and-hardening`, `forge-idea`, `party-mode`, `spec-kernel`, `correct-course`, `prd`, `prfaq`, `ux-spec`, `retrospective`); merged owners (`executing-plans` slice/impact references, `refactoring` clarity/structural/deprecation references, `requesting-code-review` review-lens/doubt references, `subagent-driven-development` parallel-dispatch reference, `source-driven-development` research references); bundle assignments in frontmatter; merged sections in `brainstorming`, `using-superpowers` (intent fork, anti-stack, tiny-edit, implementation priority, contextual gates), `test-driven-development`, `systematic-debugging`, `requesting-code-review`, `codebase-design`, `writing-plans`, `handoff`, `verification-before-completion`; private invocation and `bundle` parsing in `src/index.ts`; review-pin blocks in `assets/NOTICE.md`.

**CI gate (not README-only):** `tests/superpowers.spec.ts` `skill composition contracts` asserts `bundle` is the only catalog metadata label and locks the nineteen-skill core bundle after ADDs. Bundle tests assert the default core catalog and opt-in bundles. `fusion reference packs` asserts each fusion pack listed above exists with its defining pins. Separate gates assert every reference file is linked from its owner, every packaged Markdown file has paired code fences, and every relative Markdown link under `skills/` resolves. `catalog description contracts` asserts semantic description groups (fail), positive-segment negative boundaries that block route contradictions (fail), and positive trigger overlap among extension skills (warn only). `tests/scripts.spec.ts` executes the packaged SDD scripts in throwaway repositories. Gated skills include the discipline extension set plus the process spine (`brainstorming`, `systematic-debugging`, `verification-before-completion`, `writing-plans`, `executing-plans`, `requesting-code-review`, `subagent-driven-development`, `test-driven-development`). ADDs are not members of those semantic/overlap tables; pairwise Jaccard description collision

This bundle declares `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages. DSH checks those ranges against the running runtime at install and profile startup; an incompatible pair is refused unless the profile grants an exact `package@version` × `dsh-version` exemption. Source-workspace `workspace:*` peers mean the matching DSH release; packed manifests substitute that exact version. See the [plugin manager's compatibility reference](../../boot/plugin-manager/README.md#version-compatibility-and-exemptions) for `version-exemptions`, `allow-version`, and the crash/data-loss risk.

On every non-subagent request, `system-prompt/assemble` prepends section `skill:superpowers` whose text is `buildBootstrapPreamble(...)`: the framing below, the body of the packaged `using-superpowers` SKILL.md (frontmatter omitted), then `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md`. Agentless assemblies omit the section. `session.header.origin === 'subagent'` gets `skill:superpowers-worker` from `buildWorkerPreamble()` instead of the full bootstrap. Compaction cannot drop the guidance because it is reassembled with the system prompt each turn, not stored as a one-shot user message.

```markdown
<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

1. Call the dsh `skill` tool with the exact catalog name **before** clarifying, exploring, reading files, or acting — unless every tiny-edit condition in `using-superpowers` holds.
2. Anti-stack: load **one** process skill first; add supporting skills only when that skill delegates them or the user requires them. "Not an automatic workflow" means do not stack — not "skip `skill`".
3. Independent domains in one turn: issue multiple `subagent` / `subagent_fork` calls in the **same** assistant message.
4. After dispatch: finish only local work that does **not** need child results, then **end this turn**. Parent↔child talk uses adjacent `send_message` (Steer; tool returns delivery ack only — replies and `subagent-settled` arrive via inbox). Do **not** loop `list_agents` or status-ping `send_message` ("how is it going?") to wait.

**Below is the full content of your `using-superpowers` skill — your introduction to using skills.
For all other skills, call the dsh `skill` tool with the exact catalog name.**

[full using-superpowers SKILL.md body — frontmatter omitted]

Your harness is DeepSeek Harness. Follow this adaptation (same role as Superpowers `references/*-tools.md`):

[full dsh-tools.md]
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
```

```markdown
<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You are a Superpowers **worker** subagent.

1. Execute the dispatch brief. Do not invent a second process workflow or re-route the parent task.
One large system-prompt section on every non-subagent request; skill catalog entries add their usual summary cost when `dsh-tool-skill` is mounted.

Stable prefix for a given skills root and bootstrap toggle: the section text is loaded once at plugin apply and reused. While `bootstrap` stays enabled and the packaged preamble is unchanged, the rendered text is byte-stable so the warm prefix cache is reused. Changing `skillsRoot` or disabling `bootstrap` changes the assembled prompt.
Indirectly through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill`: every model-invocable Superpowers skill name/description in `<available_skills>`, and full bodies when loaded via `skill`.

Scales with skill count and description caps owned by `dsh-tool-skill`. The packaged catalog is 35 skills; the default core catalog is 19, of which 16 are model-invocable. Optional bundles add 16 more skills, 15 model-invocable (`grilling` is user-only). Reference packs add no catalog entries.
Same as the skill consumer: initial catalog after the reusable prefix; replacements append.

- No runtime invariant companion is published; skills are immutable packaged files and bootstrap is a `system-prompt/assemble` listener with no independently observable durable event stream. Offline turn scoring lives in `scripts/score-skill-first.mjs` (first `tool/call` of each turn vs `skill`, plus same-turn `list_agents` counts after a `subagent` / `subagent_fork` dispatch); it does not enforce behavior at runtime.
- **No upstream hook binary** — bootstrap is a Cordis `system-prompt/assemble` listener, not `hooks/session-start`.
- **A complete persona replaces every section** — an agent whose composition registers a `complete` persona (agent presets) suppresses all prompt sections, including `skill:superpowers` and `skill:superpowers-worker`, for that agent.
- **Packaged preamble must avoid `{{...}}` prompt-variable syntax** — `loadBootstrapPreamble` rejects a complete `{{name}}` group at plugin apply (mirrors skill-always-apply); a custom `skillsRoot` that introduces one fails loud before the first turn.
- **Cross-harness reference content is removed** — foreign platform tool refs, Anthropic skill-authoring guides, and harness-specific testing examples are omitted; `dsh-tools.m

The package owns skill discovery, bundle filtering, invocation metadata, and the system-prompt bootstrap. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`, `dsh-skill-filesystem`, and `dsh-tool-skill` remain upstream and unmodified.
